ordered_diagnoses: Pulmonary Atresia with Intact Ventricular Septum

facts.raw_span: A 10-day-old, 40-kg male Chianina calf
progressive dyspnea, lethargy, and recumbency
temperature was 38.5 °C
heart rate, 170 beats/min with regular rhythm
respiratory rate, 60 breaths/min
jugular pulses were present and mucous membranes were cyanotic
a grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur
severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice
a 16 mm interatrial defect in the upper septum
severe tricuspid regurgitation and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects
agitated saline contrast injected via the left jugular vein produced bubbles in the left atrium and ventricle and exiting the right ventricle through both great vessels

support_spans: a grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur
severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice
concepts.why: The combination of severe dilation of the right atrium and ventricle, a hypoplastic left ventricle, and a reduced mitral valve orifice suggests a unifying process of tricuspid atresia, where the tricuspid valve is absent or abnormally developed, leading to right-sided heart hypoplasia and decreased cardiac output.

support_spans: a grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur
a 16 mm interatrial defect in the upper septum
severe tricuspid regurgitation and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects
concepts.why: The presence of a ventricular septal defect, overriding aorta, right ventricular outflow tract obstruction, and right ventricular hypertrophy, as suggested by the murmur and septal defects, points to a unifying process of tetralogy of Fallot, a congenital heart defect characterized by four key features.

support_spans: a grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur
severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
concepts.why: The combination of a systolic murmur and severe dilation of the right atrium and ventricle suggests a unifying process of Ebstein's anomaly, a congenital heart defect characterized by an abnormal tricuspid valve and right ventricular hypoplasia.

support_spans: a 16 mm interatrial defect in the upper septum
severe tricuspid regurgitation and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects
agitated saline contrast injected via the left jugular vein produced bubbles in the left atrium and ventricle and exiting the right ventricle through both great vessels
concepts.why: The presence of two great vessels arising from the right ventricle, as suggested by the echocardiography and contrast study, points to a unifying process of double outlet right ventricle, a congenital heart defect characterized by both great vessels originating from the right ventricle.
